_meta.purpose: Immutable, append-only ledger of pre-committed LOVS methodology calibration points for the BDBV 2026 outbreak. Each block is a pin moment: a set of corridors committed on a fixed date, with a fixed model uncertainty range and a fixed resolution date. refresh_pipeline.py reads the active (unresolved) blocks and carries their points forward UNCHANGED into every snapshot; it never re-derives them from the current run's corridor ranking. That carry-forward is the pre-commitment contract the calibration scoring depends on.
doctrine: Pin once. A block's points, model ranges, pin date, and resolution date are never edited after commit.
Carry forward. A daily refresh re-emits the active points verbatim. Re-deriving them from freshly ranked corridors would silently overwrite an earlier commitment and break pre-commitment.
Append only. New calibration points are added as a NEW block at an explicit pin moment, never by mutating an existing block.
Resolve by appending. On a resolution date, score the due points against public reports and append the outcome; the original pinned range is never altered.

Early-lock when monotonic-safe. A point may have its outcome appended before its block's resolves_at iff a new lab-confirmed case appears in the target zone strictly inside [pinned_at, resolves_at]: the YES outcome is monotonic-safe (cannot flip back) and the append is structurally identical to a resolution-date append. The early-lock authorization applies only to YES outcomes; resolved_no outcomes wait for resolves_at to remove ambiguity about late-arriving evidence.
_meta.id_derivation: hypothesis_id = 'calibration-point:bdbv-uga-cod-2026:30d:' + sha256('bdbv-uga-cod-2026|{source}|{target}|{horizon_days}d|{pinned_at}')[:10]. refresh_pipeline._calibration_point_id reproduces this and verifies every point's id against its corridor at load time.

This block augments the initial top-four block with a designed sample across the current watchlist's relative high/mid/low bands, cross-border and in-country corridors, and likely positive / likely negative controls. Because the aggregate-input model still clusters all 18 watchlist corridors in a narrow probability band, these are relative tiers within the 21 May watchlist, not absolute low/medium/high probabilities.

blocks.rationale: Third calibration block. Graduates Goma (goma-cod) from geographic-anchor-not-in-calibration to a pinned candidate target on 2026-05-26 per founder direction (see .process/2026-05-26-pre-refresh-decisions/follow-up-after-pushback.md, Thread 2 path A). Pins the three Ituri source HZs -> goma-cod corridors at the ascertainment-adjusted 50% intervals from the 2026-05-26 pipeline run with goma-cod added to candidate_target_zones. Pre-pin prior context (NOT a resolution event): one laboratory-confirmed BDBV case in Goma on 2026-05-17, a woman who travelled from Ituri Province (per data/zones.json:goma-cod and data/external_sources/bdbv-2026.observed.json). Doctrine[4] early-lock will fire only on a new lab-confirmed case landing in Goma strictly inside [2026-05-26, 2026-06-25T23:59:59Z]; the 17-May case is outside that window and is therefore not a doctrine[4] trigger. Carried forward unchanged on every later refresh; scored against public reports on 2026-06-25.

blocks.rationale: Fourth calibration block. Pins the 2026-06-04 west/SSD corridor expansion: two new candidate targets (yei-ssd, kisangani-cod) graduate to pinned corridor endpoints, and the four highest-signal source-to-target corridors to them are committed at the ascertainment-adjusted 50% intervals from the 2026-06-04 pipeline run with both targets added to candidate_target_zones. yei-ssd tests northward cross-border exportation to South Sudan (West Nile / Morobo-Kaya axis); kisangani-cod tests the westward Tshopo / Congo-river axis (RN4 via Mambasa and Bafwasende), a no-PCR surveillance gap. The aru -> yei-ssd point is a designed geography-vs-load blindspot probe (frontier geography flags Aru while the case-load model rates it low). Corridor basis: WHO DON603 (2026-05-29). Carried forward unchanged on every later refresh; scored against public reports on 2026-07-04.

blocks.rationale: Block 5. The first block pinned since 2026-07-05, closing a 58-day gap in which the outbreak grew from 35 to 60 affected health zones and 6,041 confirmed cases with zero open forward commitments (public_nowcast_status.json recorded open_calibration_commitments: 0). Pre-registration cannot be backfilled, so the gap is permanent; this block restarts the clock. DESIGN CHANGE, and the reason this block exists in this shape: Blocks 1 to 4 pinned 19 points whose probability midpoints all fell in roughly 0.36 to 0.39. calibration_resolver.py's own reliability_note records the consequence -- 'reliability is effectively a single bin' -- so four blocks of pre-commitment could measure Brier but could not measure calibration. Block 5 therefore selects deterministically across SIX probability bands (very_low, low, low_mid, mid, high, very_high), two points per band, giving a midpoint range of 0.023 to 0.951. Reliability becomes measurable for the first time. The selection rule is mechanical and was fixed before the values were read: within each band take the corridors closest to the band midpoint, require a distinct (source, target) pair, and prefer an unused source and target for coverage. This also carries forward the convergent finding from the public calibration ledger's Block 4 (directional roles discriminated at 3/3 and 0/2 while the middle distance-tiers were flat at 0/2 and 0/3) and from the IDB Track B scoring of 2026-09-01 (confidence 0.80 and 0.70 calls were close to honest, 0.60 and 0.50 calls went 0 for 5). Both say the same thing: the middle is where the information is not. Spanning the range is how that gets tested rather than assumed.
blocks.registration_note: Pinned 2026-09-01 on founder go-signal, NOT backdated. Model values are read verbatim from data/live-bdbv-2026-output.json (as_of 2026-08-29T23:59:59Z, data_as_of 2026-08-29); no probability in this block is authored. LOOK-AHEAD AUDIT. Targets already carrying a confirmed case are excluded as saturated: beni-cod (136 confirmed), goma-cod (1), kisangani-cod (makiso-kisangani-cod 9, first confirmation 2026-06-30). The six eligible targets are arua-uga, bundibugyo-uga, kampala-uga, kasese-uga, nebbi-uga and yei-ssd. South Sudan has reported no confirmed case in this outbreak (WHO DON613, 17 July 2026; ECDC page updated 2026-08-31). Uganda's outbreak was declared over by WHO on 2026-08-26, so a Uganda pin is a genuine re-importation forecast rather than a restatement of an existing case; per ledger doctrine only a confirmation dated inside [pinned_at, resolves_at] resolves a point YES, so the pre-window Uganda caseload (20 cumulative) is excluded by construction. RESIDUAL RISK, stated rather than hidden: the model snapshot is data_as_of 2026-08-29 and the pin date is 2026-09-01, a three-day lag. A confirmation occurring on 30 or 31 August would not be visible here. The 2026-08-31 ECDC update was checked as the closest available audit point and showed no new Uganda or South Sudan case. Any point later found to have been pre-resolved must be retired in a dated note, never silently rescored.
